text:
The Maple Leafs are winless in eight (0-7-1) and have been outscored 33-15. Thursday's game against the Kings, lost after regulation, gave them their first point since Halloween. The hard part for anyone looking for bad luck: they've had only 43% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, in that run. This one is mostly real.

Jim Hiller's first season has gone sideways fast. At 8-13-3 with 19 points, they're 1-8-1 in their last ten, and our playoff chances for them have dropped to 2%. Sergei Bobrovsky, signed in July to be the answer in net, has lost his last five starts with a .827 save rate, 7.6 goals worse than an average goalie would allow on those shots. Strangely, the season as a whole has the opposite problem: the Leafs have scored about five goals more than their chances suggest, and our numbers still have them a few points short of what they've earned.

The noise around them is loud. Auston Matthews' future is a talking point, William Nylander's effort is being questioned on podcasts and TV, and Morgan Rielly was slated to return from injury this week. Rookie Gavin McKenna is getting his first taste of a crisis.

The bright spot is Matthews' line with Jack Roslovic and Easton Cowan, which wins its minutes 10-4. The top pair of Jake McCabe and Darren Raddysh has been outscored 14-10. If Hiller makes changes, we'd watch the blue line first.
headline: Eight games, no wins, real chances
